newsitem.title: UK: Europe veg oils close sharply lower, trade active.
newsitem.headline: Europe veg oils close sharply lower, trade active.

text.p: Heavy falls in Chicago following the release of the USDA's crop report triggered a sharply lower close on the European vegetable oil market on Friday.

The USDA estimated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.346 billion bushels, above average U.S. trade estimates of 2.287 billion bushels and higher than the U.S. government's forecast in September of 2.270 billion bushels.
Lower prices brought buyers into the market although some were still reluctant to get involved at this stage.
"Chicago opened with sharp falls, but a lot of people want to see the close before they commit themselves," said a trader.

Dutch soy oil closed 2.25 to 1.50 guilders down in a tradeless market while rape oil was 2.50 to 2.75 guilders lower after Nov/Jan traded at 96 and 95.50 and Feb/Apr at 97.75, 97 and 96.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Palm oil trade had been very slow earlier with many Far East players absent ahead of Saturday's annual Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange (KLCE) dinner.
The release of two palm oil output and stock estimates next week also made players wary with Ivan Wong's report due on Monday and PORLA's offical figures on Tuesday.
However the lower Chicago opening weighed on prices and by the close palm oil was $7.50 to $12.50 down across the board after crude palm oil fetched $527.50 a tonne for Jan/Mar cif.
RBD oil traded at $495 for Nov and palm olein at $525 for Nov, and Jan/Mar $530, $527.50 and $525 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Coconut oil closed $12.50 to $10 down after Oct/Nov traded at $727.50, Nov/Dec at $717.50, Dec/Jan at $710 and Jan/Feb at $712.50. Palmkernel oil finished $10 to $15 down in a neglected market.
